title: Safety Oracle: adaptive gating for safe batching & KV-cache rollout
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a production-safe automation layer (Safety Oracle) that recommends and applies batching and KV-cache configuration changes with SLO-anchored guardrails, plus an automated canary apply/rollback flow. The oracle should produce conservative recommendations, run staged canaries, detect anomalies in latency/throughput/quality, and automatically rollback or quarantine traffic when thresholds are breached. This ticket covers design, infra integrations, canary policy, and runbook updates.
background: We have manual and semi-automated optimizers that propose batching/kv-cache changes but lack a single coordinated safety layer enforcing latency/throughput SLOs. Recent cost-optimization attempts have caused p99 regressions during peak tails and required manual interventions. We need an automated, explainable gating system that ties recommendations to measurable SLO signals and supports safe apply/rollback across hosted and dedicated deployments.
goals: 1) Produce per-route batching and KV-cache recommendations with estimated cost delta and SLO risk. 2) Implement an adaptive gating policy that uses real-time telemetry (p50/p95/p99, throughput, cache-hit-rate, effective-batch-size) to decide whether to apply in canary, scale canary percentage, or abort. 3) Provide automated rollback/quarantine triggers and clear explanations for actions. 4) Integrate with Console dashboards, alerts, and audit logs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Safety Oracle can generate recommendations for at least 3 production routes and present expected token-cost delta and expected latency impact.
- Canary flow supports staged percentage ramp with automatic progression and automated rollback if p99 increases more than 10% or error rate increases >0.3% over baseline for 5m.
- Rollbacks are enacted automatically and captured in audit logs with root-cause indicators (latency histograms, KV hit change, batch-size distribution).
- Operators can manually pause or force-apply and see the rationale in Console.
- End-to-end tests simulate traffic spikes and nonstationary workload; system must rollback in tests that mimic recent incident patterns.
design_decisions:
- Use SLO-anchor model: baseline SLO envelope per-route derived from a 7-day rolling baseline and service-level objectives.
- Recommendation engine will prefer smaller batch size increases and cache priming before aggressive changes; rank changes by cost-benefit ratio and SLO risk score.
- Canary progression strategy: 0% -> 2% -> 10% -> 35% -> 100% with dynamic hold windows driven by a rolling anomaly detector.
- Anomaly detection: combine statistical change-point detection on p99 and p50 with EWMA on KV-hit-rate and batch-size skew metrics. Use lightweight model to maintain explainability.
- Safety gates: absolute thresholds (p99 > baseline * 1.10) and relative detectors (Z-score on p99 distribution) both required to trigger automatic rollback to reduce false positives.
- Fallback routing: if canary fails, shift canary traffic to earlier-compatible model variant or dedicated routing path to maintain availability.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for recommendation scoring and risk calculation.
- Integration tests that mock telemetry streams and verify canary progression/rollback.
- Chaos tests using traffic replay with synthetic tail latency spikes to ensure rollback sensitivity.
- A/B experiments in staging with mirrored production traffic and injected KV-hit anomalies.
- Load tests to validate controller scalability at 200k rps across 50 routes.
rollout_plan:
- Phase 1 (staging): deploy Safety Oracle in read-only mode to surface recommendations and simulated canary outcomes (2 weeks).
- Phase 2 (limited prod): enable canary execution for low-risk routes (<1% traffic, non-critical) with manual approval required to progress beyond 10% (3 weeks).
- Phase 3 (automated safe-rollouts): enable automatic canary progression for routes with stable baselines and strong test coverage; monitor closely for 2 weeks.
- Phase 4 (scale): expand to high-traffic routes and integrate with Dedicated pools; add operator training and runbook updates.
monitoring_playbook:
- Primary SLO signals: p99 latency, p95 latency, request error rate, throughput.
- Secondary signals: KV cache hit rate, effective batch size distribution, CPU/GPU utilization per pool, queueing depth.
- Alerting rules: immediate page on p99 regression >15% sustained for 2m or error rate >1% sustained for 1m.
- Canary-watch rule: when holding at a canary stage, alert on any 5m window where p99 exceeds baseline*1.10 or KV-hit-rate drops >8 percentage points.
- Post-mortem template: capture recommendation payload, pre/post histograms, canary logs, and decision timeline.
- Recovery actions: automated rollback + route pinning to previous config; operator workflow to investigate and re-run with narrower deltas.
risks_mitigations:
- Risk: false-positive rollbacks during noisy baselines. Mitigation: require multi-signal agreement and a brief hold window before rollback.
- Risk: insufficient telemetry resolution leads to noisy decisions. Mitigation: increase ingestion granularity for routes in canary to 10s buckets.
- Risk: economic regressions from over-conservative gating. Mitigation: iterative tuning, track realized unit-cost delta and incorporate into recommendation ranking.
- Risk: cross-route interference when cache priming occurs. Mitigation: namespace cache priming per-customer or per-route, simulate priming effects in staging before apply.
